label: muse-spark-1.1-noreason
caveat: Reconstructed rubric from ft-data/README.md documented criteria. The original judging prompt was never committed to this repo. Not strictly comparable to extract-gold-fable-scores.json.

audio.reasoning: Claims 1-9 are well grounded in the Q990D product pages (11.1.4 config, Dolby Atmos, Q-Symphony, speaker layout, Alexa/Google Assistant), with no cross-model contamination (Q995D forum posts correctly ignored) and no junk like star ratings extracted. Minor deduction: claims 10-11 come from generic Samsung soundbar support articles not specific to the Q990D, so attributing them as Q990D specs is slightly overreaching.

tv_display.reasoning: All claims are grounded in the source text (mostly the official Samsung QN90D product page), with no contamination from the other models mentioned in the model-selector boilerplate (QN800D, S90D, QN85D) and no junk claims like the 4.7 star rating or pricing/nav boilerplate. Minor nitpicks: the '98-inch' label for the 2.47 m variant is an inference (though accurate), and the 2-year warranty is a region-specific retail term rather than a universal product spec.

computing.reasoning: All claims are grounded in the source text and the AI features are correctly tied to the Gen 13 Aura Edition, but the extraction badly fails generation disambiguation: claims 2–10 mix Gen 13 specs (8MP MIPI camera) with Gen 12 specs (1920x1200 touch, 32GB, 1TB Gen 5 SSD, WiFi 6) without labeling which generation they belong to. It also pulled garbled retailer-listing junk from Source 7 ('max resolution 4K', '400 nits' from a fragmented spec dump) as clean product claims.

wearable_health.reasoning: All claims are grounded in the source text, the extraction correctly avoided contaminating Charge 6 with Google Fitbit Air specs (sources 4-5), and skipped junk like troubleshooting threads and video promos. Minor quibble: the ECG PDF claim comes from the generic ECG app Play Store listing rather than a Charge-6-specific source, though other sources confirm ECG is a Charge 6 feature.

kitchen.reasoning: Extraction is well grounded and correctly disambiguates Presto models (01264 aluminum, 01362 stainless, 02141 electric), while filtering out the Beddle, T-Fal, MegaChef, wine-cabinet, and star-rating junk. Minor deductions: 'safety lock lid' in claim 8 appears to come from the generic non-Presto Amazon listing (Source 12), and claims 10 and 12 aren't clearly model-attributed, risking slight generation/product blur.

cleaning.reasoning: All claims are grounded in the source text, no junk (prices, ratings, unrelated washer/phone content) was extracted, and most claims correctly label their model (Jet 60, Jet Bot Combo, AI Jet Ultra, AI Jet Lite). However, several claims lack model attribution (claims 2, 4, 7, 12), and specs from clearly different product lines (Jet 60 stick, Jet Bot Combo robot vacuum) were extracted at all for a 'Bespoke Jet Vacuum' query, creating cross-product contamination risk even with partial labeling.

power_charging.reasoning: Every claim is directly grounded in the source text (Best Buy and Newegg product descriptions), with no cross-product contamination and no junk extracted from the extensive star-rating/review boilerplate in Source 8. Claim categorization (spec vs. marketing) is sensible; only extremely minor items like price were left out.

baby.product: Dr. Brown's Natural Flow Baby Bottles
baby.reasoning: All claims are grounded in the source text, junk (prices, Amazon Live videos, competitor comparison) was correctly filtered, and there is no cross-product contamination. Minor deduction because variant-specific specs (e.g., dishwasher-safe from the 9oz wide-neck listing, 'fits most breast pumps' from the narrow listing, nipple flow levels) are presented as generic product-line claims without distinguishing wide-neck vs. narrow variants.

smart_home.reasoning: Most claims are not grounded in the source text: the resolution, 6.5 MP camera with 127° FOV, speaker/tweeter/woofer details, Ambient EQ, and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth specs appear nowhere in the sources and were evidently pulled from the model's prior knowledge. Only a few items (10-inch display, camera/mic, Google Assistant, Meet/Duo calling) are actually supported, so while nothing is contaminated from other products and junk was filtered, the pervasive hallucination severely undermines the extraction.

outdoor.reasoning: The source contains no checkable product claims for the Chute Mag: Source 1 is a video teaser plus Amazon footer boilerplate (only vague marketing phrasing like 'impressive insulation'), and Sources 2 and 3 are entirely different products (a 2.2L steel bottle and a third-party replacement lid). Returning zero claims is the honest, correct behavior, avoiding both junk extraction and cross-product contamination.
